title: prunus × lannesiana f. surugadai-odora
intro: Prunus × lannesiana f. surugadai-odora, commonly known as the Japanese Apricot, is a plant species within the Rosaceae family. This plant is known for its fragrant flowers and has been used in traditional medicine to promote overall health. The Japanese Apricot is believed to have various health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which may help to protect against cell damage and reduce the risk of chronic diseases. The bioactive constituents present in the Japanese Apricot include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which are thought to contribute to its therapeutic actions, such as anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antiviral activities.
